pieces.label: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题

lines.en: W: Hi, Alan. Sorry for not calling you back sooner. You said on the phone you had something you needed to discuss with me?
lines.zh: W: 嗨，艾伦。抱歉没能早点给你回电话。你在电话里说有件事想和我讨论？

lines.en: M: Well, to get right down to it, I'm having second thoughts about my major. With my family situation getting more complicated and the end of my university education nearing, persisting with Art History just doesn't seem the right choice.
lines.zh: M: 好吧，直说了吧，我开始重新考虑自己的专业了。随着家里的情况变得越来越复杂，而我也即将结束大学学业，坚持学艺术史似乎已经不是正确的选择了。

lines.en: W: Alan, in the last 3 years, I have heard nothing but how passionate you are about the Art History programme. You often told fellow classmates how fabulous the instructors were and that you finally felt accepted. What would cause you to abandon it?
lines.zh: W: 艾伦，过去三年里，我听到的全都是你对艺术史专业有多么热情。你经常告诉同学们这里的老师有多么出色，还说自己终于有了归属感。究竟是什么让你想放弃它？

lines.en: M: My father's current financial situation has helped me realize that a more financially viable employment opportunity is not necessarily a bad thing. Art History nourishes my soul, but does nothing to put food on my plate.
lines.zh: M: 我父亲目前的经济状况让我意识到，选择一个经济上更可行的就业机会未必是件坏事。艺术史滋养了我的心灵，却无法解决我的温饱问题。

lines.en: W: What about all the work opportunities I discussed with you last month? Have you gone to those places of business to investigate whether any legitimate positions might be available for someone with your background?
lines.zh: W: 那我上个月和你谈过的那些工作机会呢？你有没有去那些公司了解一下，看看是否有适合你这种背景的人担任的正规职位？

lines.en: M: Ah, well…
lines.zh: M: 啊，这个嘛……

lines.en: W: Look, Alan, if your heart is set on working in the art industry, you need to be more assertive and start talking with people. Networking is key if you want to become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries.
lines.zh: W: 听我说，艾伦，如果你一心想在艺术行业工作，就得更加主动，开始和人交流。如果你想成为博物馆和画廊界的名人，人脉是关键。

lines.en: M: Time is a very precious commodity right now. My social life does not exist. I can barely keep up with my studies and thesis is due by the end of this year. When can I find time to research jobs when I have so much to do as it is?
lines.zh: M: 现在时间非常宝贵。我的社交生活根本不存在。我连学业都勉强应付得来，而论文要在今年年底前提交。我已经有这么多事情要做，哪儿还有时间去研究工作呢？

lines.en: W: What you do now will determine your future options. Now is the optimum time to put forth your best effort.
lines.zh: W: 你现在所做的一切将决定你未来的选择。现在正是拿出最大努力的最佳时机。

lines.en: M: I will take what you said into consideration. The advice is much appreciated.
lines.zh: M: 我会考虑你说的话。非常感谢你的建议。

pieces.label: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题

lines.en: M: Have you decided yet what your end-of-semester business project will be on?
lines.zh: M：你决定好学期末的商业项目要做什么了吗？

lines.en: W: Yes. How about you?
lines.zh: W：决定了。你呢？

lines.en: M: Yes. Go on. You go first.
lines.zh: M：我也决定了。你先说吧。

lines.en: W: I am going to do it about beef.
lines.zh: W：我打算做牛肉方面的项目。

lines.en: M: Beef?
lines.zh: M：牛肉？

lines.en: W: Yeah, beef. I'm going to design a business case study for a cow farm that supplies beef for the domestic market.
lines.zh: W：对，牛肉。我打算为一家向国内市场供应牛肉的养牛场设计一份商业案例研究。

lines.en: M: Well, that sounds very interesting and original. Wherever did you get that idea?
lines.zh: M：听起来确实很有意思，也很有新意。你到底是怎么想到这个点子的？

lines.en: W: I don't know. It just came to me, I guess. But think about it. Beef consumption has been rising strongly over the past 20 years. As the economy continues to grow, consumer demand is expected to continue to increase for the foreseeable future. And currently, most of the beef is imported, which brings with it added fees. So why not raise cattle here?
lines.zh: W：我也不知道。我想大概就是突然想到的吧。不过你想想，过去20年来，牛肉消费量一直在大幅增长。随着经济持续发展，预计在可预见的未来，消费者的需求还会继续增加。而且目前大部分牛肉都是进口的，这还会带来额外的费用。所以，我们为什么不在这里养牛呢？

lines.en: M: Of course. Makes perfect sense. There's plenty of land out west. So, if done right, it should be very profitable to raise our own cattle.
lines.zh: M：当然可以。完全说得通。西部有的是土地。所以，只要经营得当，自己养牛应该会非常赚钱。

lines.en: W: Exactly.
lines.zh: W：没错。

lines.en: M: Seriously, that sounds like a great idea. You should genuinely look into it once we get our degrees.
lines.zh: M：说真的，这听起来是个很棒的主意。等我们拿到学位后，你确实应该好好研究一下。

lines.en: W: Thanks. So, your turn now. What are you doing your case study on?
lines.zh: W：谢谢。现在轮到你了。你的案例研究要做什么？

lines.en: M: I was thinking about a car wash, but it now seems like such a boring notion after hearing your brilliant idea.
lines.zh: M：我原本在考虑洗车店，但听了你这个绝妙的主意后，我的想法现在显得太无聊了。

lines.en: W: That's cool. I could see that working. After all, there's plenty of cars about and those aren't going away any time soon. While many people don't care how their car looks, many other people do. You got yourself a vast and continual market.
lines.zh: W：这想法不错。我觉得能行。毕竟，车很多，而且短期内也不会减少。虽然很多人不在乎自己的车看起来怎么样，但也有很多人在乎。这样一来，你就拥有了一个庞大而持续的市场。

lines.en: M: Right. So the idea is a large self-cleaning car wash, but I mean really big and well-outfitted like they have in America. I was thinking of having it cater to high-end consumers in large cities. It could charge a profitable markup by offering just a bit more technical equipment and professional service than competitors.
lines.zh: M：对。所以我的想法是开一家大型自助洗车店，不过要像美国那种真正规模很大、设备齐全的洗车店。我考虑让它面向大城市里的高端消费者。只要比竞争对手多提供一些技术设备和专业服务，就可以收取有利可图的溢价。

pieces.label: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题

lines.en: Increased television time for young children has long been linked with poorer progress in some areas of development. One possible way to counter those negative effects is talking while watching the screen. As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten. This was particularly true for children with socioeconomic disadvantages.
lines.zh: 长期以来，幼儿看电视时间增加一直与其在某些发展领域进步较差有关。抵消这些负面影响的一种可能方式是在观看屏幕时进行交谈。一项新研究表明，父母在电视时间与学龄前儿童进行的对话越多，这些儿童进入幼儿园时表现出较高好奇心水平的可能性就越大。对于处于社会经济劣势的儿童而言，这一点尤其明显。

lines.en: "Our findings reinforce the importance of parent conversation to promote early childhood development and curiosity," said lead author Prachi Shah at University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital. Researchers assessed hours of daily television exposure and frequency of parent-screen-time conversation among 1,500 preschoolers, and then measured early childhood curiosity in kindergarten. The study specifically focused on curiosity levels, which are associated with enhanced learning and higher academic achievement in reading and math at kindergarten, and behavioral-developmental benefits, especially for children from families with lower socioeconomic status. While many young children are now growing up with digital media exposure through mobile devices like tablets and phones, television remains a dominant screen activity, accounting for 72% of all screen time. TVs are in 98% of all homes, keeping television exposure a relevant developmental context in young children.
lines.zh: 密歇根大学健康中心C.S.莫特儿童医院的首席作者普拉奇·沙阿说：“我们的研究结果进一步证明，父母的对话对于促进幼儿早期发展和好奇心十分重要。”研究人员评估了1500名学龄前儿童每天接触电视的时长，以及父母在屏幕使用期间与孩子交谈的频率，随后测量了这些儿童进入幼儿园时的早期好奇心。该研究特别关注好奇心水平，因为好奇心与幼儿园阶段更强的学习能力、更高的阅读和数学学业成就，以及行为和发展方面的益处相关，尤其是对来自社会经济地位较低家庭的儿童而言。如今，许多幼儿通过平板电脑和手机等移动设备接触数字媒体，但电视仍然是主要的屏幕活动，占全部屏幕使用时间的72%。所有家庭中有98%拥有电视，这使电视接触仍然是幼儿发展中一个重要的环境因素。

lines.en: Excessive media exposure, including television, can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent-child interactions, which are believed to be key to cultivating curiosity in kids. "Our findings suggest the importance of parents finding opportunities to foster conversational exchanges in daily routines with their young children—including while watching television," Shah said.
lines.zh: 过度接触媒体，包括看电视，可能会挤占游戏和亲子互动等探索性活动，而这些活动被认为是培养儿童好奇心的关键。沙阿说：“我们的研究结果表明，父母应当在日常生活中寻找机会与幼儿进行对话交流，包括在观看电视时进行交流。”

pieces.label: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题

lines.en: Humans are aspirational goal-seeking beings. Each of us, according to research, has an inborn drive to acquire. The "dark side" of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more "things" and to socially compare our "stuff" with all the stuff other people have in their lives. So the question is, how do we ensure we tap into our drive to acquire in positive ways that will benefit our well-being?
lines.zh: 人类是有抱负、追求目标的存在。研究表明，我们每个人天生都具有获取的驱动力。这种获取驱动力的“阴暗面”，在于不假思索地驱使自己拥有越来越多的“东西”，并将自己的“财物”与他人生活中拥有的一切进行社会比较。因此，问题在于，我们该如何确保以积极的方式运用这种获取驱动力，从而增进自身的幸福感？

lines.en: One way is to become more intentionally aspirational. To be intentionally aspirational includes consciously aspiring to be the person you need to be to succeed in your professional and personal life. It also includes consciously aspiring to acquire things in your life that will positively impact your sense of well-being. If you're not consciously, mindfully and intentionally harnessing this inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.
lines.zh: 一种方法是更加有意识地树立抱负。有意识地树立抱负，包括自觉追求成为一个能够在职业生活和个人生活中取得成功所需要成为的人。这也包括自觉追求获得生活中那些能够积极影响你幸福感的事物。如果你没有有意识、专注而明确地驾驭这种与生俱来的获取驱动力，就可能会在不假思索地追求所有错误的事物。

lines.en: While your intentional aspirational goals will include pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well-being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles. Your intentional aspirational goals will also include striving to be your personal best—a person of "good" character, integrity, and trustworthiness.
lines.zh: 虽然你有意识树立的抱负目标会包括追求获得能够提升幸福感的事物，但这些目标也应包括在你所承担的各种生活角色中帮助他人的目标。你有意识树立的抱负目标还应包括努力做到最好的自己，成为一个具有“良好”品格、正直而值得信赖的人。

lines.en: Think about this from a practical, rather than theoretical viewpoint. If you're not pursuing intentional aspirational goals, you have nothing to strive for. If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you will not be able to experience, live and enjoy all that life has to offer.
lines.zh: 请从实际而非理论的角度思考这一点。如果你没有追求有意识树立的抱负目标，就没有任何目标可供努力。如果你没有任何目标可供努力，就会使自己处于一种危险境地，只是在生活中随波逐流，也就无法体验、生活并享受人生所能提供的一切。

pieces.label: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题

lines.en: It's revision time for exams and dissertations. The pressure is on, so you want all the help you can get to aid your memory and raise your grades. As a nutrition expert, I want to say that eating well can make a real difference to your revision regime—so what brain-boosting food and drink would I recommend?
lines.zh: 现在是准备考试和论文的复习阶段。压力很大，因此你希望得到一切可能的帮助来增强记忆力、提高成绩。作为一名营养专家，我想说，吃得健康能让你的复习安排产生显著不同，那么我会推荐哪些能增强大脑功能的食物和饮品呢？

lines.en: Coffee can have numerous benefits. However, while coffee may make you more alert, individuals can build up a tolerance, meaning this is short-lived. Coffee can also increase blood sugar and eventually cause lack of focus and energy. It's also worth noting that people react differently to coffee. Some people can drink it at midnight and go straight to sleep, whereas others get feelings of anxiety after a small amount. Also remember that coffee from a coffee shop may be stronger than coffee made at home. So stop drinking coffee by 2 pm and have a maximum of 2 cups of coffee a day, but be aware of your own reaction to it.
lines.zh: 咖啡有许多益处。然而，虽然咖啡可能会让你更加警觉，但人们会逐渐产生耐受性，这意味着这种效果是短暂的。咖啡还会升高血糖，最终导致注意力和精力不足。同样值得注意的是，人们对咖啡的反应各不相同。有些人可以在午夜喝咖啡后直接入睡，而另一些人只喝少量咖啡就会感到焦虑。还要记住，咖啡店的咖啡可能比家里冲的咖啡浓。因此，下午两点后就不要再喝咖啡了，每天最多喝两杯，但要留意自己对咖啡的反应。

lines.en: Whole grain foods will ward off hunger. Examples include porridge and whole wheat bread. Combining whole grain foods with protein will help keep your blood sugar levels balanced, which is essential for mood and concentration. Berries and nuts are a convenient and nutritious snack. Blueberries, like many dark colored fruits and vegetables, can slow down brain damage and age-related decline. Frozen berries are also a good choice. They are usually cheap, last longer and don't lose their nutrients when frozen. But flavored and coated nuts are less healthy as they contain added oil, salt, and sugar.
lines.zh: 全谷物食品可以防止饥饿。例子包括粥和全麦面包。将全谷物食品与蛋白质搭配食用，有助于保持血糖水平平衡，而这对情绪和注意力至关重要。浆果和坚果是方便又有营养的零食。蓝莓和许多深色水果、蔬菜一样，可以减缓大脑损伤和与年龄相关的衰退。冷冻浆果也是不错的选择。它们通常价格便宜、保存时间更长，而且冷冻后不会损失营养成分。但调味坚果和裹层坚果不那么健康，因为其中含有额外添加的油、盐和糖。

lines.en: Doctors often recommend taking vitamin supplements to top up on the nutrients you need. But I would say food should always come before supplements and the key to getting as many nutrients as possible is to eat a varied diet with lots of different colors such as frozen berries and dark green vegetables. It's better to get everything you need from food and drink. For example, oranges contain not only vitamin C which boosts the immune system, but also fiber and other components that you can't get packaged together in a tablet.
lines.zh: 医生经常建议服用维生素补充剂，以补充你所需的营养物质。但我认为，食物始终应该优先于补充剂，而获得尽可能多营养的关键，是食用包含多种不同颜色食物的多样化饮食，例如冷冻浆果和深绿色蔬菜。最好从食物和饮品中获取你所需要的一切。例如，橙子不仅含有能增强免疫系统的维生素C，还含有纤维和其他无法在一片药片中同时获得的成分。

lines.en: Don't forget to drink a proper amount of water, which can boost attention by almost 25 percent and can elevate your mood as well.
lines.zh: 别忘了饮用适量的水，这可以将注意力提高近25%，也能改善你的情绪。

lines.en: Finally, don't skip meals. Eating regularly will help keep blood sugar balanced and feed the brain with the fuel it needs.
lines.zh: 最后，不要不吃饭。规律进食有助于保持血糖平衡，并为大脑提供所需的能量。

pieces.label: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题

lines.en: The late Swedish academic Hans Rosling has identified a worrying trend: not only do many people across advanced economies have no idea that the world is becoming a much better place, but they actually even think the opposite. This is no wonder, when the news focuses on reporting catastrophes, terrorist attacks, wars, and famines.
lines.zh: 已故瑞典学者汉斯·罗斯林发现了一个令人担忧的趋势：不仅许多发达经济体中的人们根本不知道世界正在变得越来越美好，实际上他们甚至认为情况恰恰相反。当新闻集中报道灾难、恐怖袭击、战争和饥荒时，这也就不足为奇了。

lines.en: Who wants to hear about the fact that every day some 200,000 people around the world are lifted above the $2-a-day poverty line? Or that more than 300,000 people get access to electricity and clean water for the first time every day? These stories in people in low-income countries simply don't make for exciting news coverage. But, as Rosling pointed out in his book Factfulness, it's important to put all the bad news in perspective.
lines.zh: 谁愿意听到这样的事实：世界各地每天约有20万人脱离每日2美元的贫困线？或者每天有超过30万人首次用上电并获得清洁饮用水？这些关于低收入国家民众的故事，确实难以成为令人兴奋的新闻报道内容。但是，正如罗斯林在他的《事实》一书中指出的那样，重要的是要把所有坏消息放在整体背景下加以看待。

lines.en: While it is true that globalization has put some downward pressure on middle-class wages in advanced economies in recent decades, it has also helped lift hundreds of millions of people above the global poverty line. If we really care about global welfare, globalization is the only way forward to ensure that economic prosperity is shared among all countries and not only a select few advanced economies.
lines.zh: 诚然，近几十年来，全球化对发达经济体中产阶级的工资造成了一定的下行压力，但它也帮助数亿人脱离了全球贫困线。如果我们确实关心全球福祉，那么全球化就是确保经济繁荣惠及所有国家，而不仅仅是少数发达经济体的唯一前进道路。

lines.en: While some people glorify the past, one of the big facts of economic history is that until quite recently a significant part of the world population has lived under quite miserable conditions—and this has been true throughout most of human history.
lines.zh: 虽然有些人美化过去，但经济史的一大事实是，直到相当晚近的时候，世界人口中仍有相当一部分生活在十分悲惨的条件下，而这在绝大部分人类历史时期一直如此。

lines.en: While there were many long-lasting ups and downs, like the Great Depression or the recent Great Recession, the constancy of the long-run growth rate is actually quite miraculous. Low-income countries, including China and India, have been growing at a significantly faster pace in recent decades and are quickly catching up to the West. A 10% growth rate over a prolonged period means that income levels double roughly every seven years. It is obviously good news if prosperity is more shared across the globe.
lines.zh: 尽管长期以来经历了许多持续时间较长的起伏，例如大萧条或近期的大衰退，但长期增长率的稳定性实际上相当不可思议。包括中国和印度在内的低收入国家，近几十年来一直以明显更快的速度增长，并且正在迅速追赶西方。长期保持10%的增长率，意味着收入水平大约每七年翻一番。如果繁荣能够在全球范围内得到更广泛的共享，这显然是个好消息。

lines.en: While inequality within countries has gone up as a result of globalization, global inequality has been on a steady downward trend for several decades. This is mostly a result of the improvement of hundreds of millions of people's living standards. In fact, for the first time ever since the Industrial Revolution, about half of the global population can be considered middle class.
lines.zh: 虽然全球化导致各国内部的不平等程度上升，但几十年来，全球不平等一直呈稳步下降趋势。这主要是数亿人的生活水平得到改善的结果。事实上，这是自工业革命以来，全球人口中约有一半首次可以被视为中产阶级。

pieces.label: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题

lines.en: We all know that the sense of smell is powerful. The delicious scent of bread, for example, can act like a time machine. One sniff can bring back a memory from many years ago. Indeed, scent particles, in general, can revive memories that have been long forgotten. But why do smells sometimes trigger powerful memories, especially emotional ones? The short answer is that the brain regions that handle smells, memories and emotions are linked.
lines.zh: 我们都知道，嗅觉的力量十分强大。例如，面包的诱人香气就像一台时光机。闻一下，就能唤回许多年前的一段记忆。事实上，气味分子通常能够唤醒那些早已被遗忘的记忆。但为什么气味有时会触发强烈的记忆，尤其是情感记忆呢？简而言之，负责处理气味、记忆和情感的大脑区域彼此相连。

lines.en: A scent is a chemical particle that floats in through the nose and into the region of the brain responsible for smell, where the sensation is first processed into a form that the brain can read. Brain cells then carry that information to the area of the brain where emotions are processed, and then to an adjacent area of the brain where learning and memory formation take place.
lines.zh: 气味是一种化学微粒，它经由鼻腔飘入大脑中负责嗅觉的区域，在那里，这种感觉首先被处理成大脑能够读取的形式。随后，脑细胞将这些信息传递到负责处理情感的大脑区域，再传递到相邻的、负责学习和记忆形成的大脑区域。

lines.en: Scents are the only sensations that travel such a direct path to the emotional and memory centers of the brain. That results in an intimate connection between emotions, memories and scents, which is why memories triggered by scents are experienced as more emotional than those triggered by sight or sound.
lines.zh: 气味是唯一能够沿着如此直接的路径到达大脑情感中枢和记忆中枢的感觉。这就形成了情感、记忆和气味之间的密切联系，也正因如此，气味触发的记忆往往比视觉或听觉触发的记忆更具情感色彩。

lines.en: Let's take a closer look at how those memories are activated. Usually, when a person smells something that's connected to a meaningful event in their past, they'll first have an emotional response to the sensation and then a memory might follow. But sometimes, the memory doesn't come to the surface. The person might feel the emotion of something that happened in the past but won't remember what they experienced. What causes this baffling phenomenon? The explanation is context. Imagine this scenario—a person is walking down the street smelling a scent that they first encountered decades ago, which activates an emotional response. If the person had first come across that smell in a very different context, it will be much more difficult to recover the associated memory, because the brain uses the context to give meaning to the information and find that memory.
lines.zh: 让我们更仔细地看看这些记忆是如何被激活的。通常，当一个人闻到某种与过去某个重要事件有关的气味时，他首先会对这种感觉产生情绪反应，随后记忆可能会浮现出来。但有时，记忆并不会浮现。这个人可能会感受到过去发生的某件事所带来的情绪，却想不起自己当时经历了什么。是什么导致了这种令人困惑的现象？答案在于情境。想象这样一个场景：一个人走在街上，闻到一种他几十年前第一次接触到的气味，这激活了他的情绪反应。如果这个人当初是在一个截然不同的情境中第一次闻到这种气味的，那么他就会更难回忆起与之相关的记忆，因为大脑会利用情境赋予信息意义，并找出那段记忆。

lines.en: The special nature of memories brought back by scents notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories. They aren't always accurate, and they can change over time. In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted. But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren't.
lines.zh: 尽管气味唤回的记忆具有特殊性，但它们也存在与其他记忆相同的缺陷。它们并不总是准确的，而且会随着时间发生变化。事实上，每当我们回忆某件事时，那段记忆都有可能被扭曲。但是，由于这些记忆唤起了强烈的情感联系，那些因某种气味而回忆起某件事的人往往坚信自己的记忆是准确的，即使事实并非如此。
